title: CliSubcommand
description: A verb's declaration: src/main/cli/<command>/<verb>.json. Its filename is the verb, and its directory is the command, so neither is a field here. Subcommands render in listing order, which is alphabetical - the filesystem offers no other, and that is why ordering stops being a check.

explanation.description: What the verb's things or steps are, by topic (issues/795) - what reads the same in every room. The help says what the verb is for; this says the rest, each topic one sentence or the topics beneath it. `corpus-yoga <command> -h` and the walk show them beneath the verb's summary.

help.description: The one-line description of what this verb does, shown beneath the command's forms.

would.description: What the verb would do, in the words every status says it in (issues/1028): a status names the act as the command and what it acts on, and reads these words from here - one home for them. An acting verb - one with w, x, sends or consumes - declares them.

modality.description: Whether the room must or may run the act, in RFC 2119's words (issues/1050): MUST where the room fails a property some check states until the act runs - every such verb one status satisfy runs - and MAY where the act waits on the reader's choice. A status says each act it names under now:, beneath its modality, and nowhere else. A verb that declares would declares this.

step.description: Names the pipeline this verb is a corpus-wide step of, when it is one. src/main/cli/pipeline/pipeline.sh --plan must invoke it by command AND verb (G10).

log.description: This verb writes its own run log under tmp/logs/<command>/<verb>/, so the dispatcher's derived logging (issues/453: a verb with declared w or sends leaves an anchored log) stands down for it.

args.description: The verb's arguments, in the order they render in its usage.

r.description: Reads (issues/29): repo-relative path prefixes this declaration reads - the r of the rwx triad. A row names the narrowest prefixes that cover what the code opens - two narrow rows before one wide one - since a prefix nothing under it is read by says nothing, and covers a stale literal as readily as a live one (effects.extent_covered reads rows against literals). The entry is a claim the gate may hold.

w.description: Writes (issues/29): repo-relative path prefixes this declaration writes - the w of the triad. effects.writers_disjoint holds that no prefix is claimed by two commands, exactly or by containment.

consumes.description: Consumes (issues/687): repo-relative path prefixes this declaration removes after reading - a dequeue, the fourth row of the triad. A consumed prefix is another command's to write: the room's stage, tmp/stage/input, which the captures fill and the promote verbs take from, the orphan cache subtrees the cleaner removes. effects.writers_disjoint holds w prefixes disjoint across commands; a consumes prefix overlaps a producer's w by nature and is held instead to be read by the same declaration.

x.description: Invokes (issues/29): canonical invocation forms this declaration executes - tools and parametrised commands, the x of the triad. Wire-class x's remain in sends until the census folds them in.

runs.description: The outward call as typed - a command's words, the args the script supplies following them, or the python call it makes.

refused.description: What CORPUS_YOGA_NO_SEND=1 does to it - it fails the act where the send is the work, and degrades a report to unverified where the send only enriches it.

does.description: What the send does, one entry per occasion.

sends.description: The outward calls this declaration makes (issues/29, issues/1022), keyed by name - a script runs a send by its name alone (src/main/send.py, src/main/send.sh), so a name the declaration lacks cannot run and the call has one home. A send has no scratch form: redirecting where the result lands does not stop the call going out, so CORPUS_YOGA_NO_SEND=1 refuses it.
